metaDescription: Six 1 HP dust collectors compared on rated airflow, motor construction, bag filtration and mounting, plus what a one-horsepower unit can and cannot do.
expertTake: The Shop Fox W1727 is the pick for a small shop that wants a plain 800 CFM workhorse on a 120 or 240 volt circuit, and the VEVOR wall unit is the value choice. Buyers expecting a one-horsepower machine to feed a planer through long duct runs should skip the category and look at a cyclone.
introParagraphs: One horsepower is the traditional entry rung in woodworking air movement. It is the size of motor that plugs into a household circuit, fits on a small steel base and costs far less than a cyclone, which is why so many hobby shops start here.

Horsepower on its own tells you little. Two machines with identical motors can differ by hundreds of cubic feet per minute depending on impeller design, hose size and filter, so this guide compares what each unit does with its motor rather than the motor itself.

products.name: SHOP FOX W1727 1 HP Portable Dust Collector, 800 CFM
products.description:
The W1727 earns the top slot on a clear spec: an 800 CFM rating from a motor that draws 9 amps at 120 volts or 4.5 amps at 240. Being prewired for household current but convertible to 240 volts means it fits a standard garage outlet today and can be rewired to run cooler on a higher voltage later.

What you give up is capacity detail. There is no wall mount and the layout is a classic portable single-stage machine with a bag stack, so fine dust control depends on the bag you fit. Against the VEVOR wall unit at 560 CFM it moves roughly forty percent more air, though it needs a floor spot rather than a stud wall.

The practical ownership tip is to treat the electrical conversion seriously. A 9-amp draw on a shared garage circuit can trip a breaker if a compressor is on the same line, so check the circuit before relying on it. Keep the bag clamped tight and shake the upper bag between sessions.
products.bestFor: A small shop that wants a straightforward 800 CFM unit and the option to wire to 240 volts.
pros: 800 CFM rating is the highest in a 1 HP class here
Dual voltage wiring gives electrical flexibility
Portable base rolls between machines
Modest 9 amp draw at 120 volts
cons: No wall mount for tight floor space
Bag fineness depends on the filter you fit

products.name: JET DC-650 1 HP Dust Collector, 650 CFM, Machine Base
products.description:
The JET DC-650 is the quiet one, with a single-stage design the maker puts at around 70 dB. It is designed to serve one to three machines, which is an honest statement of what a 1 HP unit can do, and it rides on four casters for easy movement.

The listing is for the machine base only, which means it ships without the bag set. Plan to buy filter and collection bags as part of the cost, and decide on the micron rating yourself. At 650 CFM it moves less air than the Shop Fox 800 CFM unit, but its lower noise makes it the one you can run through long sanding sessions without leaving the room.

JET machines tend to be built around serviceable parts. Check the bag fittings when you first assemble it, and use a short hose to protect the 650 CFM. It is an easy machine to like in a shared garage where noise complaints are a real consideration.
products.bestFor: A shared garage or basement where a quiet single-stage machine matters.
pros: Single-stage design runs at about 70 dB
Four casters for easy movement
Can serve up to three machines
115 or 230 volt operation
cons: Sold as a base only, so bags are extra
650 CFM is lower than the top 1 HP rivals

products.name: Rikon 60-100 1 HP Dust Collector, TEFC Motor, Steel Base
products.description:
The Rikon is built around a totally enclosed fan-cooled motor. A TEFC motor keeps dust out of the windings, which matters in a machine whose entire job is to move dust, and it lengthens the motor's life compared with open-frame types.

A sturdy steel base on four casters supports the machine, and a lockable toggle switch stops accidental or unauthorized starting. That last detail suits a home with children or a shared shop. The listing does not state a CFM figure in the data we saw, so confirm airflow with the seller; it should sit in the same range as other 1 HP single-stage units.

Keep an eye on the bag system and wipe the motor housing so fan cooling air can move. Unlike the JET, this is a machine you buy for durability rather than the last decibel, and it suits an owner who plans to keep it a decade.
products.bestFor: A shop that values motor durability and a lockable switch over specification detail.
pros: Totally enclosed motor resists dust
Steel base with four casters
Safety lock toggle prevents casual starting
Established woodworking brand
cons: Airflow figure should be confirmed with the seller
Basic single-stage design needs a good filter bag

products.name: POWERTEC 1 HP 800 CFM Dust Collector, 1 Micron Upper Bag
products.description:
This POWERTEC matches the Shop Fox on 800 CFM but adds a 1 micron upper bag and a caster base around 15 by 25 inches. Finer filtration is the reason to pick it, because a 1 micron bag returns much less fine dust to the room than the coarse bags that ship with many machines.

It shares the standard weakness of a fine bag, which is that it loads faster and needs more regular cleaning. It also does not offer the wiring flexibility of the Shop Fox. Compared with the VEVOR at 560 CFM it moves more air but takes up floor rather than hanging on a wall.

Shake the upper bag often and check the lower bag zip and the clamp rings. If you wire it to a shared circuit, avoid long extension cords because motors of this class dislike voltage drop.
products.bestFor: A woodworker whose priority is capturing fine dust at 800 CFM.
pros: 1 micron upper bag catches fine dust
800 CFM rating matches the best 1 HP rivals
Includes both bags
Rolls on a sturdy caster base
cons: Fine bag loads faster and needs more cleaning

products.name: VEVOR 1 HP 560 CFM Wall-Mount Collector, 21-Gallon Bag
products.description:
The VEVOR hangs on a wall, which frees the floor, and it pairs a 560 CFM rating with a 21 gallon non-woven bag and a 2.5 micron filter. The bag is the largest in this guide's wall-mount group, and the filtration is finer than the typical 5 micron bag.

The trade-off is fixed position. Once the bracket is up, the machine stays on one wall, so hose runs get long, and 560 CFM does not leave much margin. It suits a small shop with a bench saw and a drill press clustered together.

Mount it to studs rather than drywall anchors because a loaded bag is heavy and vibration loosens weak fasteners. Empty the bag at the halfway mark and look over the non-woven cloth for pinholes.
products.bestFor: A compact shop with machines grouped along a single wall.
pros: Wall mount keeps the floor clear
21 gallon bag is generous
2.5 micron filter beats a 5 micron bag
Low cost for a 1 HP unit
cons: 560 CFM leaves little margin on long hoses

products.name: POWERTEC 1 HP 560 CFM Wall-Mount Collector, 1 Micron Bag
products.description:
This is POWERTEC's wall version of its 560 CFM machine, shipped with a mounting bracket and a reusable 1 micron bag with a window and a zipper. It is compact and aimed at small shops that value filter quality over flow.

Against the VEVOR it uses a finer bag but a smaller capacity, and both share the 560 CFM rating. The window helps you empty before suction drops, which is a small feature that prevents a lot of lost performance.

Use a stud, empty outdoors, and keep the hose short. It is the machine to buy when a 1 micron bag matters and the collector must hang out of the way.
products.bestFor: A small shop that wants fine filtration from a wall-hung unit.
pros: 1 micron bag with a dust-level window
Includes a mounting bracket
Reusable bag with zipper emptying
Compact for a 1 HP machine
cons: 560 CFM limits it to one small tool at a time

buyingCriteria.explanation: A one horsepower motor is enough for one tool at a time on a short hose. The Shop Fox at 800 CFM and the JET at 650 CFM both advertise serving more than one machine, but only by moving the hose between them. Chaining a planer and a saw through a long run will starve any 1 HP machine, and buyers who need that should look at a larger motor.

At 120 volts the Shop Fox draws 9 amps, which is a meaningful share of a 15 amp garage circuit. Dual voltage units such as the Shop Fox and JET can be rewired to 240 volts, drawing half the current. If a compressor or heater shares the circuit, check the load before you rely on a collector.

Dust collectors live in the dust they move. The Rikon uses a totally enclosed fan-cooled motor that keeps debris out of the windings, which prolongs life. Open-frame motors are common on cheaper bag machines. If you plan to keep the machine for a decade, enclosure matters more than a small CFM difference.

The POWERTEC machines use 1 micron bags, the VEVOR a 2.5 micron filter and a 21 gallon bag, while the JET ships without bags at all. Fine bags protect lungs but clog sooner. Capacity matters because a bag past half full loses suction. Match the bag to how much sanding versus sawing you do.

Casters let the Shop Fox, JET and Rikon follow the work and keep hoses short, which preserves CFM. Wall units like the VEVOR and POWERTEC 560 CFM free the floor but fix the position. In a tiny shop the floor space is worth more than the mobility.

A collector runs alongside the loudest tool in the shop, so its own noise stacks on top. The JET is quoted at roughly 70 dB, quieter than many small units. If you work in a shared space, noise controls how long you can run it, so that figure is worth reading.

specDecoder.meaning: A motor rating that hints at power but not airflow. Impeller and housing design set the real output.
specDecoder.watchFor: Every machine here is 1 HP yet they range from 560 to 800 CFM.

specDecoder.meaning: Totally enclosed fan cooled, a motor sealed against dust with an external cooling fan.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Rikon 60-100 uses one, which is uncommon at this price.

specDecoder.meaning: The motor can be wired for 120 or 240 volts, halving the current at the higher voltage.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Shop Fox and JET offer it, the POWERTEC and VEVOR do not.

specDecoder.meaning: The finest particle the filter is designed to stop. Smaller means finer and faster loading.
specDecoder.watchFor: The POWERTEC bags are 1 micron, the VEVOR filter 2.5 micron.

specDecoder.meaning: A listing that sells the motor and housing without bags or hoses.
specDecoder.watchFor: The JET DC-650 listing is base only, so bags add to the cost.

howWeEvaluated.title: Airflow within the class
howWeEvaluated.description: All six share a 1 HP motor, so we compared stated CFM and judged how it survives a hose. The Shop Fox at 800 CFM and POWERTEC 800 CFM lead, with the wall units at 560 CFM trailing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor construction
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at enclosure, voltage options and likely noise. The Rikon TEFC motor and the JET 70 dB single-stage design stand out, while the voltage flexibility of the Shop Fox earns credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration and bags
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared micron ratings and bag capacity. The POWERTEC 1 micron bags and the VEVOR 21 gallon bag score best, and the JET loses points for shipping without bags.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mounting and space
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed caster bases against wall brackets for small shops. Mobile units keep hoses short, while wall units save floor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership practicality
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered switches, handles, service parts and the likelihood of leaks. The Rikon lockable switch and the POWERTEC dust window are small features that matter over years.

Cramped shop, machines on one wall
Base only but quiet and well made

cards.label: Caster base
cards.text: The Shop Fox, JET, Rikon and POWERTEC 800 CFM roll to the machine, so hose runs stay short and airflow stays high. They cost floor space and need a flat, clear route.

cards.label: Wall mount
cards.text: The VEVOR and POWERTEC 560 CFM wall units free the floor but fix their position. Longer hose runs eat into a 560 CFM rating quickly.

howToChoose.note: Choose casters if your tools move; choose a wall unit if your tools stay put.

howToChoose.subheading: For a Small Woodworking Shop Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a machine sized to one tool at a time with a short hose, a fine bag you can empty outdoors and a switch you can reach. Avoid chasing the highest quoted CFM.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Shop Fox W1727 gives the best balance of airflow and electrical flexibility, and the POWERTEC 800 CFM is the pick if fine dust worries you most.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you plane lumber or run several tools; a 1 HP machine, even the Shop Fox, will not keep up and a larger motor is the better investment. Spend more also for the Rikon enclosed motor if you plan decades of use.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you saw and sand lightly. The VEVOR wall unit with a 21 gallon bag handles that work and keeps the floor clear.

maintenance.why: Suction falls as the bag fills. Empty outdoors with a respirator on.
Fine bags pack with dust and cut airflow. Shake it out away from the shop.
Loose clamp rings leak fine dust into the room. Check the lower bag zipper too.
Dust on the housing blocks cooling. TEFC motors rely on an external fan, so keep it clear.
Wall units carry a heavy full bag, and caster units shed sawdust into the wheels.

faq.q: Is 1 HP enough for a woodworking shop?
faq.a: It is enough for one tool at a time with a short hose. A planer or several tools on long ducts need a larger motor. Treat 1 HP as the small-shop size.

faq.q: Can I run a 1 HP unit on a normal outlet?
faq.a: Yes, at 120 volts it draws about 9 amps on the Shop Fox. Do not share the circuit with a compressor or heater. A 240 volt option halves the current.

faq.q: Does a bigger bag improve performance?
faq.a: A bigger bag lasts longer between empties and keeps suction steadier. It does not raise the maximum airflow. Fine bags still load faster than coarse ones.

faq.q: Why does the JET ship without bags?
faq.a: Some listings sell only the machine base. You must buy bags separately and choose a micron rating, so budget for it.

faq.q: Is a TEFC motor worth it?
faq.a: For long service life in a dusty room, yes. It keeps debris away from the windings. It does not change airflow.

faq.q: What about ducting with a 1 HP unit?
faq.a: Keep runs short and use smooth pipe or short hose. Every bend costs airflow, and a 1 HP machine has little to spare.
